title: Llama 3.2-Vision 11B Instruct
name: Llama 3.2-Vision 11B Instruct
description: Llama 3.2-Vision 11B Instruct is Meta’s production multimodal checkpoint for image understanding, document analysis, captioning, and assistant-style question answering over image+text inputs.

downloads.notes: Official checkpoint and license entry point.

runtime_compatibility.notes: Official model card shows Transformers usage for image+text input.
Meta release materials position these as official local/on-device paths for Llama 3.2.
Meta release blog lists single-node distribution via Ollama.
Community support exists; verify current multimodal compatibility against runtime docs.
Supported through ecosystem conversion workflows for NVIDIA deployments.

deployment.recommended_quantization: Use BF16 for production image understanding when possible; use quantization only when memory budget is the gating constraint and you have validated image tasks on your workload.

license_info.name: Llama 3.2 Community License
license_info.notes: The license governs multimodal use, redistribution, required attribution, and the commercial threshold; the model card also notes an EU restriction for multimodal models.

best_for: Document understanding workflows with charts, tables, and layout-heavy images.
Visual question answering and captioning services.
Multimodal assistants that need image+text input and text output in production.
avoid_for: Text-only chat where a smaller Llama text checkpoint will meet quality needs.
Ultra-low-memory edge devices that cannot handle a vision adapter and image tokens.
High-throughput pipelines that do not need image understanding and would pay unnecessary multimodal overhead.
engineering_snapshot.recommended_use_case: production multimodal inference for image understanding and document-centric assistants.
deployment_risks: Multimodal serving overhead including image preprocessing, adapter execution, and image-token memory.
Degraded accuracy or compatibility issues under aggressive quantization without validation.
failure_modes: Tokenization/adapter mismatch in runtimes that lack proper multimodal support.
Silent quality regression or OOM failures when processing complex or multi-image documents.
common_mistakes: Attempting multi-image or unsupported multilingual image workflows without systematic validation.
Sizing memory allocation purely based on text-only footprint without planning for vision-token memory inflation.
operational_notes: The model uses a separately trained vision adapter with cross-attention into the base Llama 3.1 language model, so image-token handling is part of the inference cost model and not an optional feature.

Meta positions 11B Vision for local, on-prem, cloud, and on-device distributions through Llama Stack, ExecuTorch, and partner ecosystems, which means deployment planning should include both accelerator choice and adapter-compatible runtime selection.

The release notes recommend device-specific distribution paths and note BF16 weights; quantized variants were discussed as future work, so compression should be treated as an optimization layer rather than the baseline deployment mode.

The model card documents image+text prompting with Transformers 4.45.0+, and the release blog notes that only English is officially supported for image+text applications, which affects international deployment scope.

Variant differentiation (Identity): this variant is the family’s mid-size vision checkpoint, optimized for image reasoning and doc-style workflows, while remaining substantially easier to serve than 90B.

Variant differentiation (File Formats): because this is a vision-language model, format support is less universal than text-only Llama checkpoints and often depends on runtime-specific multimodal adapters.

Variant differentiation (Hardware Requirements): 11B vision sits in the “serious single-node multimodal” band — far more feasible than 90B, but still expensive enough that image token handling and KV cache planning matter.
Variant differentiation (Downloads): the official Hugging Face repo is the practical distribution point, while Meta’s download page governs access and licensing.
Variant differentiation (Runtime Compatibility): this variant requires a runtime that handles both the language model and the vision adapter path; “text-only compatible” is not sufficient.

Variant differentiation (Deployment): multimodal serving introduces image preprocessing, adapter execution, and image-token memory overhead, so deployment risk is higher than for text-only checkpoints of similar size.
Variant differentiation (License): because this is multimodal, the license has extra deployment implications beyond the text-only family, especially for geographic and product distribution policy.
Variant differentiation (Status): this is a released production checkpoint with explicit multimodal support, not an experimental adapter demo.

Variant differentiation (Engineering Snapshot): the main decision is not just model size but whether you need a vision stack at all; if yes, 11B is the family’s most practical quality/feasibility balance.

Variant differentiation (Engineering Notes): 11B Vision is the first Llama 3.2 tier where multimodal correctness is a core product risk, so input policy and runtime validation matter as much as raw model selection.
